FactSet News Alert for: 



Headline: StreetAccount Macro Update: Weekend Headlines
Source: 
Identifier(s): 

Date & Time: 12:04 PM 4 Oct '26

  • Iran war:
       • Iran maintains Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until seven conditions from June interim agreement are satisfied
         (Reuters)
       • At least two vessels struck over weekend in waters near Oman, Iran (CNBC)
       • Houthis claimed responsibility for drone and ballistic missile strike on Aramco facility in Riyadh on Saturday
         (Reuters)
       • Iran faces economic collapse as US blockade and inflation pressure the regime (Bloomberg)
       • Saudi Arabia plans major counteroffensive against Houthis though US declines to join operation (Axios)
  • Energy:
       • OPEC+ maintains oil production targets for November amid ongoing regional conflict (Reuters)
       • Iraq rearranges transits to offer oil outside the Persian Gulf, pursuing alternative export outlets (Bloomberg)
  • AI:
       • Global AI infrastructure spend projected to hit $30T by 2050, rivaling total value of outstanding US Treasuries
         (Reuters)
       • White House launches Super Intelligence Force led by Director of National Intelligence Clayton to assess AI risks,
         maintain US leadership (Bloomberg)
       • AI startup Reflection preparing to release open-weight system that could threaten both Chinese, US AI giants (Axios)
  • Markets:
       • Treasury Secretary Bessent dismisses concerns over rising bond yields as global trend, says he can't control bond
         market but can slow down investors' decisions (Bloomberg)
       • Wall Street IPO momentum stalls as investor demand cools, valuation concerns mount (FT)
       • Investors ignore elevated yields, continue to plow into AI-linked stocks (Bloomberg)
       • Investors seek portfolio diversification to hedge against rising concentration risks in AI (FT)
       • Average high-grade US corporate bond yield tops 6% for first time since 2023 (Bloomberg)
       • German government bonds rally as safe haven in global bond rout (FT)
       • Traders fear contagion in European bond markets after French debt selloff (Bloomberg)
       • Surging global bond yields weigh on European stocks as equity risk premium rises to 7.1% (Bloomberg)
       • Investors stick with EM carry trade following first quarterly loss in two years on US Treasury yield surge, dollar
         rally (Bloomberg)
  • Trade/tariffs:
       • China launches anti-dumping probe into European chemical exports amid rising trade tensions (FT)
       • US to receive first shipment of Belarusian potash in four years as sanctions ease (FT)
  • Geopolitics:
       • Ukraine to target Russian oil refineries in response to Moscow's new winter airstrike campaign (Reuters)
       • Russia threatens to intensify infrastructure strikes after Ukraine refinery threat (Bloomberg)
  • Central banks:
       • Cleveland's Hammack says Fed still has a lot of information to come before October decision (Reuters)
  • Economy:
       • US sees five-straight months of flat or negative wage growth, adding to latest consumer concerns (link)
       • US consumers maintain spending despite inflation outpacing wage growth for five consecutive months (Bloomberg)
       • US EV demand shows signs of stabilization as gasoline prices remain elevated (Bloomberg)
  • Corporate:
       • OpenAI's Altman says Cerebras a close partner, will continue to have deep engagement with AI chipmaker (CNBC)
       • Berkshire Hathaway increases stake in Lennar to 11.2% though buying pace slows (CNBC)
       • Wall Street investors grow wary of intertwined debt risks between Oracle and Paramount (Bloomberg)
       • Airbnb's Chesky says platform unlikely to allow AI agents to book accommodations (Nikkei)
       • US to loan Vistra ~$4.2B to boost nuclear power generation (Reuters)
